findings.title: FLUIDSIM_OT_apply_capacity_suggestion modifies RNA properties and domain transforms but lacks UNDO in bl_options
findings.description: The operator declares bl_options = {"REGISTER"} (line 191) without "UNDO". Its execute method modifies multiple scene RNA properties via setattr(fs, name, value) (line 305) and modifies the domain object's location and dimensions via _apply_domain_bounds (lines 180-181: domain.location = ..., domain.dimensions = ...). These are standard Blender undoable data types. Without UNDO, Blender does not push an undo step for this operator, so pressing Ctrl+Z after approving capacity changes undoes whatever step preceded the approval, leaving stale fs.* settings and domain transforms that no longer match the running solver. The operator has explicit rollback logic (lines 316-319) for failures, confirming these are recognized as significant mutations.
findings.impact: Users who approve capacity changes cannot revert them through Blender's undo system. They must manually undo each property change and domain resize, risking a desync between scene settings and the live solver state.

findings.title: FLUIDSIM_OT_export_cache_sequence lacks poll() guard, button always enabled without active solver
findings.description: Unlike FLUIDSIM_OT_export_frame (line 1448) which inherits _FLUIDSIM_OT_session_base (providing a poll that requires an active solver), FLUIDSIM_OT_export_cache_sequence (line 1483) inherits only bpy.types.Operator and defines no poll method. The 'Export Cache Sequence' button in the Output panel (panels.py line 1008) is therefore always enabled regardless of solver state. When clicked with no active solver, bridge.session().export_cache_sequence(scene, start, end) at line 1508 fails and is caught by the generic except at line 1509, producing an error report rather than the correct UX of a greyed-out button.
findings.impact: Users can click an export button that cannot succeed, receiving a generic error instead of a visually disabled control. This is misleading about what actions are available.
findings.fix: Either inherit _FLUIDSIM_OT_session_base or add a poll classmethod that returns False when bridge.session().active is False.

findings.title: FLUIDSIM_OT_toggle_live has no bl_options, making the live-mode toggle non-undoable
findings.description: FLUIDSIM_OT_toggle_live (line 518) declares no bl_options at all. Its execute method sets fs.live = True/False and fs.status (lines 537-541). Because no undo step is pushed, pressing Ctrl+Z after toggling live on will undo whatever step preceded the toggle while fs.live remains True. Additionally, the operator lacks a poll() guard but is designed to self-initialize the solver (lines 530-536). The Simulation panel greys out the toggle via row.enabled = sess.active (line 216), hiding functionality the operator actually supports when invoked directly.
findings.impact: The live simulation toggle is non-undoable, so users cannot revert it through standard Blender undo. The greyed-out UI also misrepresents the operator's capabilities since it can initialize the solver on its own.
findings.fix: Add bl_options = {"REGISTER", "UNDO"}. Consider whether the panel enable logic at line 216 should be relaxed to reflect the operator's self-initialization capability.

findings.title: FLUIDSIM_OT_apply_pending_reinitialize and FLUIDSIM_OT_apply_pending_reset declare REGISTER without UNDO despite modifying scene settings
findings.description: FLUIDSIM_OT_apply_pending_reinitialize (line 395, bl_options = {"REGISTER"}) calls _bridge().apply_pending_reinitialize(context.scene) at line 410, which modifies scene-level RNA properties. FLUIDSIM_OT_apply_pending_reset (line 426, bl_options = {"REGISTER"}) similarly calls _bridge().apply_pending_reset(context.scene) at line 449. Neither includes "UNDO" in bl_options. The RNA property changes made by these bridge methods are not captured in an undo step, so they cannot be reverted through Blender's undo system. Compare with FLUIDSIM_OT_revert_pending (line 465) which correctly declares {"REGISTER", "UNDO"} for its RNA modifications.
findings.impact: Restart/reset-tier pending settings applied through these operators are non-undoable. Users must manually revert each changed setting if they want to roll back.
findings.fix: Add "UNDO" to bl_options for both operators.

findings.title: Snippet line-edit operators silently return CANCELLED without user feedback when no active snippet exists
findings.description: FLUIDSIM_OT_snippet_edit_line.invoke (line 1384) returns {"CANCELLED"} when _active_snippet(context) returns None. FLUIDSIM_OT_snippet_edit_line.execute (line 1393), FLUIDSIM_OT_snippet_line_add.execute (line 1420), and FLUIDSIM_OT_snippet_line_delete.execute (line 1438) also return {"CANCELLED"} without calling self.report(). No error or warning message is shown to the user. While the Snippet Editor panel (panels.py lines 1093-1094) does show 'Add or load a snippet first' text, the operators themselves fail silently if invoked through search menu or API.
findings.impact: Users invoking these operators outside the panel context get no feedback about why nothing happened.
findings.fix: Add self.report({'WARNING'}, 'No active snippet') before each bare return {"CANCELLED"}.

findings.title: FLUIDSIM_OT_step and FLUIDSIM_OT_release declare no bl_options, leaving fs.status changes outside the undo system
findings.description: FLUIDSIM_OT_step (line 486) and FLUIDSIM_OT_release (line 117) declare no bl_options at all. Both modify context.scene.fluidsim.status (step at line 513 via sess.error, release at line 125). While the primary effect of these operators is on external GPU solver state (which cannot be undone), the RNA property changes to fs.status are also not captured in any undo step. This means status text changes persist through undo operations, potentially showing stale status after an undo.
findings.impact: Minor: status text may become stale relative to actual solver state after undo operations. Not a functional defect since GPU state cannot be undone regardless.
findings.fix: Consider adding bl_options = {"REGISTER"} to both operators so Blender tracks them in the operator stack, even if UNDO is intentionally omitted for solver lifecycle operations.
